blocks.text: Imagine a world where software changes are deployed to production multiple times a day with minimal risk. This is the promise of Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Delivery (CD).

blocks.markdown: Continuous Integration (CI) is a software development practice where developers frequently integrate their code changes into a shared repository. Each integration is verified by an automated build and test process. This practice helps to identify integration issues early and reduce the risk of defects in the software.

blocks.title: Continuous Integration
blocks.text: Continuous Integration is the practice of automatically building and testing code changes frequently, ideally multiple times a day.

blocks.markdown: A typical CI pipeline consists of several stages: **Source Code Management**, **Build**, **Test**, and **Deploy**. Each stage serves a specific purpose in ensuring the quality and reliability of the software.

rows: Manage and track changes to the codebase.
Compile the source code into executable artifacts.
Run automated tests to verify the functionality of the code.
Deploy the code to a production-like environment for further testing.
blocks.caption: Stages of a Continuous Integration Pipeline

blocks.markdown: CI reduces integration risk by ensuring that code changes are tested in isolation and as part of the entire system. This frequent testing helps to catch defects early, reducing the time and cost associated with fixing them.

blocks.title: Integration Risk Reduction
blocks.text: By frequently integrating and testing code changes, CI helps to identify and fix defects early, reducing integration risk.

blocks.title: Example CI Pipeline
blocks.prompt: Consider a development team working on a web application. They use a CI pipeline to automate their workflow. Let's explore how this pipeline works.

steps.text: 1. A developer commits code changes to the version control system (e.g., Git).
2. The CI server detects the change and triggers the build stage.
3. The build stage compiles the code and generates an executable.
4. Automated tests are run to verify the new functionality.
5. If all tests pass, the code is deployed to a staging environment for further testing.

blocks.answer: The CI pipeline automates the process of building, testing, and deploying code changes, ensuring that defects are identified early.

blocks.markdown: For Continuous Deployment (CD) to be safe, certain preconditions must be met: comprehensive automated testing, robust monitoring, and a rollback mechanism. These ensure that any issues in production can be quickly identified and resolved.

blocks.title: Preconditions for Safe CD
blocks.text: Ensure comprehensive automated testing, robust monitoring, and a rollback mechanism before implementing Continuous Deployment.

blocks.title: Safe Continuous Deployment
blocks.prompt: A company wants to implement Continuous Deployment for their mobile app. What steps should they take to ensure safety?

steps.text: 1. Implement comprehensive automated tests covering all critical functionalities.
2. Set up robust monitoring to detect issues in real-time.
3. Develop a rollback mechanism to revert deployments if necessary.

blocks.answer: By ensuring these preconditions, the company can safely deploy changes to production, minimizing risk.

points: CI involves frequent integration and testing of code changes to reduce integration risk.
A typical CI pipeline includes stages such as Source Code Management, Build, Test, and Deploy.
Safe Continuous Deployment requires comprehensive testing, monitoring, and rollback mechanisms.
